ideas.title: Single press-and-hold button

new_nodes.label: Clockwork timer knob
new_nodes.detail: 0-30 min mechanical dial with bell

new_nodes.label: Hold-to-heat button
new_nodes.detail: Magnetron runs only while finger is on one big button

new_nodes.label: Set cooking duration
new_nodes.detail: User decides how long to heat

ideas.rationale: No settings at all: press means heat, release means stop, which nobody needs to learn.

ideas.title: Foot pedal timer

new_nodes.label: Foot pedal
new_nodes.detail: Sewing-machine style pedal replaces timer knob; harder press = more power

new_nodes.label: Set cooking duration
new_nodes.detail: Hands-free intuitive control

ideas.rationale: Borrows a universally understood pedal metaphor and frees hands holding the plate.

ideas.title: Hourglass timer

new_nodes.label: Sand hourglass switch
new_nodes.detail: Flip the glass; a light sensor stops the magnetron when sand runs out

new_nodes.label: Optical sand-level sensing
new_nodes.detail: Cheap phototransistor at base of glass

ideas.rationale: Everyone already knows how an hourglass works; time is literally visible.

ideas.title: Door-close-starts-cooking

new_nodes.label: Door latch start switch
new_nodes.detail: Closing the door starts heating; opening stops it; fixed 60 s burst

new_nodes.label: Door push-release button
new_nodes.detail: Existing mechanical door opener

ideas.rationale: Removes the start step entirely; the only action is putting food in.

ideas.title: Weight-based auto timer

new_nodes.label: Spring scale turntable
new_nodes.detail: Turntable sits on spring; heavier load = longer fixed cam time

new_nodes.label: Infer cooking duration from mass
new_nodes.detail: No user input needed

ideas.rationale: Replaces the timer knob with a mechanical scale so the user sets nothing.

ideas.title: Steam-stop sensor replaces timer

new_nodes.label: Humidity cutoff sensor
new_nodes.detail: Stops heating when cavity humidity spikes, i.e. food is hot

new_nodes.label: Capacitive humidity sensing
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost sensor in exhaust duct

ideas.rationale: The microwave knows when food is done, so there is no duration to learn or guess.

ideas.title: IR food-temperature cutoff

new_nodes.label: Infrared thermopile
new_nodes.detail: Reads surface temp; stops at 70 °C eating temperature

new_nodes.label: Heat to eating temperature
new_nodes.detail: Outcome-based instead of time-based

ideas.rationale: The user asks for 'hot', not minutes and watts.

ideas.title: Two-button Hot/Warm

new_nodes.label: Hot / Warm buttons
new_nodes.detail: Two big tactile buttons replace both knobs with fixed presets

new_nodes.label: Power knob
new_nodes.detail: Existing 5-step duty-cycle cam

ideas.rationale: Reduces every decision to one binary choice in plain words.

ideas.title: Coin-slot style token timer

new_nodes.label: Minute-token slot
new_nodes.detail: Drop plastic tokens, each = 1 minute, mechanical counter advances

ideas.rationale: Counting physical tokens is more intuitive than reading a dial scale.

ideas.title: Pull-string timer

new_nodes.label: Pull-cord retract timer
new_nodes.detail: Pull cord out like a talking doll; retraction speed sets time

new_nodes.label: Escapement spring retractor
new_nodes.detail: Same clockwork, different interface

ideas.rationale: Length pulled is a visible, bodily measure of time with no numbers.

ideas.title: Mug-size shaped cavity

new_nodes.label: Cup-shaped mini cavity
new_nodes.detail: Cavity fits a mug only; fixed power and time for one beverage

new_nodes.label: Reheat a drink
new_nodes.detail: Single-purpose appliance

ideas.rationale: Form dictates use so there is nothing to configure.

ideas.title: Dial with pictograms only

new_nodes.label: Pictogram dial
new_nodes.detail: Replaces minute scale with icons: cup, plate, pizza, popcorn mapping to cam positions

ideas.rationale: Users match a picture to their food instead of estimating minutes.

ideas.title: Voice-only control

new_nodes.label: Offline voice module
new_nodes.detail: 'Heat my soup' parsed by keyword chip; no buttons or knobs

new_nodes.label: Edge speech recognition
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost keyword-spotting MCU

ideas.rationale: Speaking a wish is the lowest possible learning curve.

ideas.title: Barcode cooks the packet

new_nodes.label: Barcode reader window
new_nodes.detail: Wave package at door; lookup table sets time/power

new_nodes.label: 1D barcode scanning
new_nodes.detail: Commodity scanner module

ideas.rationale: Packaging already knows the instructions, so the user never reads them.

ideas.title: Bimetal auto-stop

new_nodes.label: Bimetal cavity thermostat
new_nodes.detail: Cuts magnetron when exhaust air hits set temperature; no timer at all

new_nodes.label: Bimetallic strip switching
new_nodes.detail: Cents-level cost

ideas.rationale: Cheaper than a clockwork timer and needs no user setting.

ideas.title: Transparent casing, no lamp

new_nodes.label: Metal-mesh glass cavity
new_nodes.detail: Full transparent cavity walls with fine Faraday mesh; ambient light only

new_nodes.label: Interior incandescent lamp
new_nodes.detail: Existing 20-25 W bulb

ideas.rationale: Seeing food from any angle removes the mental model of a hidden box.

ideas.title: Open-top toaster microwave

new_nodes.label: Choke-sealed top slot
new_nodes.detail: Drop plate through top like a toaster; lever starts and pops up when done

new_nodes.label: Quarter-wave choke seal
new_nodes.detail: Leak suppression without hinged door

ideas.rationale: Reuses the universally known toaster lever gesture.

ideas.title: Drawer instead of door

new_nodes.label: Slide-out drawer cavity
new_nodes.detail: Pull drawer, place food, push closed to start

ideas.rationale: Push-to-start on close removes the door button and start step.

ideas.title: Kitchen-timer twist egg

new_nodes.label: Detachable egg timer
new_nodes.detail: Standard twist egg timer docks on top and is the only control

ideas.rationale: Uses an object people already own and understand.

ideas.title: Colour-coded cups

new_nodes.label: RFID cookware tags
new_nodes.detail: Branded bowls carry tag; microwave reads it and cooks preset

new_nodes.label: NFC reading
new_nodes.detail: Antenna under turntable

ideas.rationale: The dish carries the settings so the user carries none.

ideas.title: Loudness bell to talking bell

new_nodes.label: Mechanical bell
new_nodes.detail: Existing end-of-cycle bell

new_nodes.label: Chime-and-voice chip
new_nodes.detail: Says 'Done, careful it's hot'

ideas.rationale: Explains the state rather than making users decode a sound.

ideas.title: Light = heat indicator

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic door panel
new_nodes.detail: Door glass tints red while cavity is hot, no lamp

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic film
new_nodes.detail: Passive, zero electronics

ideas.rationale: State is communicated by colour without any display to read.

ideas.title: Turntable removed by mode stirrer

new_nodes.label: Glass turntable
new_nodes.detail: Existing rotating plate

new_nodes.label: Fan mode stirrer
new_nodes.detail: Flat fixed floor; stirrer blade spreads field

ideas.rationale: No plate to align or wedge means no setup errors.

ideas.title: Gesture-free proximity start

new_nodes.label: Load presence switch
new_nodes.detail: Micro-switch under floor starts a 90 s cycle when weight detected and door shuts

ideas.rationale: Cooking begins automatically with zero controls.

ideas.title: Smartphone as the only panel

new_nodes.label: Bluetooth control-less chassis
new_nodes.detail: No knobs; phone app shows photos of food to tap

new_nodes.label: BLE link
new_nodes.detail: Removes all mechanical UI parts

ideas.rationale: Uses a UI people already know and updates it over time.

ideas.title: Dumb inverter power knob to slider

new_nodes.label: Fader slider
new_nodes.detail: Linear slide 'gentle ↔ strong' replaces 5-step cam

ideas.rationale: Linear more/less is grasped instantly compared to numbered steps.

ideas.title: Single knob merging time and power

new_nodes.label: Compound cam knob
new_nodes.detail: One knob: turning further = longer and stronger

ideas.rationale: Halves the controls to one monotonic dial.

ideas.title: Camera doneness vision

new_nodes.label: Cavity webcam
new_nodes.detail: Also replaces lamp via IR LED; tiny classifier detects boiling/bubbling and stops

new_nodes.label: Embedded image classification
new_nodes.detail: MCU-level model

ideas.rationale: Visual judgement is outsourced to the device.

ideas.title: Microphone pop detector

new_nodes.label: Acoustic popcorn sensor
new_nodes.detail: Stops when pops slow; also detects boiling splatter

ideas.rationale: Listening replaces user timing for noisy foods.

ideas.title: Candle-style burn timer

new_nodes.label: Fusible minute strip
new_nodes.detail: Disposable fuse strip lengths = minutes; burns through to stop

ideas.rationale: Wildly simple consumable: tear a length, insert, done.

ideas.title: Water-clock timer

new_nodes.label: Drip cup timer
new_nodes.detail: Fill a cup; drip-through float switch ends heating

ideas.rationale: Fill level is an intuitive analogue for duration.

ideas.title: Door window as whole front

new_nodes.label: Full-front mesh door
new_nodes.detail: Entire front is transparent mesh glass, no control panel at all

ideas.rationale: Removes the panel that intimidates; controls go to one top button.

ideas.title: Magnetic lid instead of latched door

new_nodes.label: Magnet-held choke lid
new_nodes.detail: Lift-off lid with magnetic seal and interlock; no hinge, no button

ideas.rationale: Lid-like access is as familiar as a saucepan.

ideas.title: Tactile Braille-free big knob

new_nodes.label: Oversized click knob
new_nodes.detail: One palm-sized knob with 4 loud detents labelled by raised icons

ideas.rationale: Few, physical, loud positions are learnable by feel in seconds.

ideas.title: Continuous low power only

new_nodes.label: Fixed 350 W magnetron
new_nodes.detail: Removes power knob; everything heats gently with one timer

ideas.rationale: Eliminating power choice removes the hardest concept to learn.

ideas.title: Plate-shaped slot

new_nodes.label: Horizontal plate slot
new_nodes.detail: Insert dinner plate like a CD; spring-loaded eject when done

ideas.rationale: Single affordance; nothing to open, nothing to set.

ideas.title: Printed instruction window

new_nodes.label: Glass-etched cheat chart
new_nodes.detail: Door glass printed with food → knob-position chart

ideas.rationale: Cheap substitute for a manual, always in view.

ideas.title: Door light from outside

new_nodes.label: External LED edge-lit door
new_nodes.detail: LEDs in door frame shine through glass; no cavity lamp or socket

ideas.rationale: Simpler service, brighter view, fewer parts.

ideas.title: Smart plug energy timer

new_nodes.label: Timed mains plug
new_nodes.detail: Microwave is always 'on'; a plug-in timer on the cord is the only control

ideas.rationale: Replaces internal timer with a familiar external one.

ideas.title: Doneness ribbon

new_nodes.label: Mechanical progress ribbon
new_nodes.detail: Coloured ribbon winds out of slot showing time left, replaces dial scale

ideas.rationale: Remaining time becomes a visible length.

ideas.title: Rotary phone dial

new_nodes.label: Return-spring finger dial
new_nodes.detail: Dial a digit of minutes; spring return starts it

ideas.rationale: Dialling a single number is self-explanatory and self-starting.

ideas.title: Self-labelling knob by lid

new_nodes.label: Snap-on preset caps
new_nodes.detail: Knob caps with words 'Coffee','Dinner' that mechanically limit range

ideas.rationale: User chooses a word, the cap does the setting.

ideas.title: Weight+IR fully blind oven

new_nodes.label: Zero-control sealed box
new_nodes.detail: No door window, no lamp, no knobs: scale + IR sensor decide everything

ideas.rationale: The most radical reduction: nothing to see or set.

ideas.title: Steam-whistle done signal

new_nodes.label: Exhaust whistle
new_nodes.detail: Kettle-style whistle in vent sounds when steam flows, replacing bell

ideas.rationale: Kettle whistle is a globally understood 'it's ready' cue.

ideas.title: One-minute cam only

new_nodes.label: Fixed 60 s push timer
new_nodes.detail: Button pushes a cam for exactly 1 min; press again for more

ideas.rationale: Counting presses beats reading a scale.

ideas.title: Door as the knob

new_nodes.label: Door-angle timer
new_nodes.detail: How far you swing the door before closing winds the timer

ideas.rationale: Merges loading and setting into one motion.

ideas.title: Tilt the oven

new_nodes.label: Rocking base timer
new_nodes.detail: Tilt the whole unit back to wind a pendulum timer

ideas.rationale: Playful whole-body gesture, no panel.

ideas.title: Heat-sensitive sticker on plate

new_nodes.label: Reusable temp sticker
new_nodes.detail: Sticker on turntable edge changes colour; user stops when colour matches

ideas.rationale: Visible done-ness replaces numeric planning.

ideas.title: Shared preset dial from kettle

new_nodes.label: Kettle-style rocker switch
new_nodes.detail: One rocker, clicks off automatically like a kettle

ideas.rationale: Copies the simplest kitchen control that exists.

ideas.title: Window-less camera mirror

new_nodes.label: Periscope mirror window
new_nodes.detail: Angled mirrors show cavity from top; cheaper than perforated glass and lamp

ideas.rationale: Viewing from above is a natural pot-watching posture.

ideas.title: Self-opening door at end

new_nodes.label: Spring auto-open latch
new_nodes.detail: Timer release pops the door open when done; replaces bell and button

ideas.rationale: An open door is the clearest possible 'done' signal.

ideas.title: One-button 'Heat It' with IR doneness sensor

new_nodes.label: Single HEAT button
new_nodes.detail: One pushbutton replaces timer and power knobs; cooking stops automatically.

new_nodes.label: IR thermopile surface-temperature sensing
new_nodes.detail: Non-contact sensor reads food surface temperature through a waveguide-safe window.

ideas.rationale: Zero settings to understand: press once, food stops when hot.

ideas.title: Hold-to-heat dead-man button

new_nodes.label: Momentary hold-to-heat paddle
new_nodes.detail: Magnetron runs only while the user holds the paddle; release stops it instantly.

ideas.rationale: Nothing to set or read; the user's own hand is the timer.

ideas.title: Toaster-style lever microwave

new_nodes.label: Spring-loaded pop-up lever
new_nodes.detail: Push lever down to start; it pops up with a click when done, like a toaster.

ideas.rationale: Borrows a control everyone already knows from toasters.

ideas.title: Pictogram food dial replaces power and time

new_nodes.label: Food-icon selector dial
new_nodes.detail: Dial positions are pictures (mug, plate, pizza slice, frozen block) mapped to fixed power/time pairs.

ideas.rationale: Users pick what they have, not watts and minutes.

ideas.title: Turntable is a weighing scale that sets the time

new_nodes.label: Load-cell turntable support
new_nodes.detail: Three load cells under the turntable ring weigh the food and compute heating duration.

new_nodes.label: Strain-gauge load cells
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost strain gauges with simple amplifier.

ideas.rationale: Put food in, close door, it already knows how long.

ideas.title: Steam-sensor auto-stop replaces the clockwork timer

new_nodes.label: Cavity humidity sensor
new_nodes.detail: Detects steam burst from food and ends the cycle.

ideas.rationale: No timer to misjudge; food tells the oven when it is done.

ideas.title: Barcode scanner reads the packet's instructions

new_nodes.label: Door-mounted barcode scanner
new_nodes.detail: Reads packaged-food barcode and applies the printed heating program automatically.

new_nodes.label: Machine vision
new_nodes.detail: Optical code reading.

ideas.rationale: Students never read the back of the box; the oven does it for them.

ideas.title: RFID smart containers set the program

new_nodes.label: RFID reader in cavity floor
new_nodes.detail: Tagged mugs/bowls carry their own heating profile; the oven applies it on door close.

ideas.rationale: The container is the interface, so no control panel is needed.

ideas.title: Voice-only control

new_nodes.label: Offline speech-command module
new_nodes.detail: Recognises 'heat', 'defrost', 'stop' without cloud.

new_nodes.label: Speech recognition
new_nodes.detail: Keyword spotting on microcontroller.

ideas.rationale: Talking is the only interface with truly no learning curve.

ideas.title: Single 'more/less' knob merges time and power

new_nodes.label: Unified heating-amount knob
new_nodes.detail: One knob scales total energy delivered; firmware picks power/time combination.

ideas.rationale: Two confusing knobs become one intuitive 'how much' control.

ideas.title: Colour-band timer scale instead of minutes

new_nodes.label: Green/amber/red timer dial
new_nodes.detail: Dial printed with coloured zones labelled 'warm', 'hot', 'cook' instead of numbers.

ideas.rationale: Replaces numeric estimation with a glanceable traffic-light scale.

ideas.title: Mug-count scale on the timer

new_nodes.label: Timer dial marked in mugs/plates
new_nodes.detail: Scale reads '1 mug, 2 mugs, 1 plate' instead of minutes.

ideas.rationale: Units match the student's mental model of what they are heating.

ideas.title: Two-position power switch (defrost / full)

new_nodes.label: Rocker switch: Defrost / Heat
new_nodes.detail: Replaces 5-step cam with a simple two-way rocker.

ideas.rationale: Removes four meaningless power steps nobody understands.

ideas.title: Fixed-power oven with no power knob at all

new_nodes.label: Hard-wired 100% duty magnetron drive
new_nodes.detail: Delete cam and knob; only a timer remains.

ideas.rationale: Cheaper and simpler: one knob, one decision.

ideas.title: Inverter power supply replaces transformer, diode and doubler

new_nodes.label: Switch-mode HV inverter
new_nodes.detail: High-frequency SMPS drives the magnetron with continuous, variable power and no large HV capacitor.

ideas.rationale: True continuous power lets a single slider mean exactly what it says, with no stored lethal charge.

ideas.title: Solid-state GaN RF source replaces the magnetron

new_nodes.label: GaN solid-state microwave generation
new_nodes.detail: Low-voltage transistor amplifiers with reflected-power feedback for closed-loop heating.

new_nodes.label: RF power electronics
new_nodes.detail: Solid-state amplifier design.

ideas.rationale: Reflected-power feedback makes auto-stop reliable, so the user never sets anything.

ideas.title: Thermal fuse replaces bimetal thermostat

new_nodes.label: One-shot thermal fuse on magnetron
new_nodes.detail: Cheaper, non-resettable thermal cut-off.

ideas.rationale: Lower cost and fewer parts keeps the product simple and affordable for students.

ideas.title: Capacitor-free design eliminates bleed-down

new_nodes.label: Resonant inverter without storage capacitor
new_nodes.detail: No energy stored after switch-off; bleeder resistor and warnings removed.

ideas.rationale: Removes a hidden hazard and its warning labels, making the product worry-free.

ideas.title: Mode-stirrer fan replaces turntable and motor

new_nodes.label: Waveguide mode stirrer
new_nodes.detail: Rotating metal paddle in the waveguide spreads the field; flat cavity floor, no turntable.

ideas.rationale: No plate to misalign, break or clean; square dishes just fit.

ideas.title: Rotating antenna under the floor

new_nodes.label: Sub-floor rotating radiating antenna
new_nodes.detail: Antenna spins beneath a flat ceramic floor to even out heating.

ideas.rationale: Flat floor removes the ‘did I seat the turntable?’ failure mode.

ideas.title: Airflow-driven turntable (no motor)

new_nodes.label: Cooling-fan-driven turntable turbine
new_nodes.detail: Magnetron cooling air spins a small turbine under the plate; no separate motor.

ideas.rationale: Fewer parts and cheaper, keeping the basic model basic.

ideas.title: Silicone mat replaces glass turntable

new_nodes.label: Microwave-safe silicone turntable mat
new_nodes.detail: Unbreakable, dishwasher-safe, rolls up.

ideas.rationale: Nothing to shatter or drop; one less thing to think about.

ideas.title: Ceramic glass plate replaces mica waveguide cover

new_nodes.label: Glass-ceramic waveguide window
new_nodes.detail: Wipe-clean non-porous cover; no mica that chars or absorbs grease.

ideas.rationale: Users never need to learn about replacing a mica sheet.

ideas.title: Magnetic door with Hall-effect interlocks

new_nodes.label: Magnetic door catch + Hall sensor interlock
new_nodes.detail: Door held by magnets; redundant Hall sensors replace mechanical microswitches and latch hooks.

new_edges.from: Magnetic door catch + Hall sensor interlock
Magnetic door catch + Hall sensor interlock
Magnetic door catch + Hall sensor interlock

ideas.rationale: Pull the door like a fridge; no button to find.

ideas.title: Pull-handle door replaces push-release button

new_nodes.label: Fridge-style pull handle
new_nodes.detail: Handle directly lifts the latch hooks; button and lever deleted.

ideas.rationale: Everyone knows how to open a door with a handle.

ideas.title: Drawer-style cavity replaces hinged door

new_nodes.label: Pull-out cavity drawer
new_nodes.detail: Food sits in a drawer that slides into the shielded box; choke is on the drawer rim.

ideas.rationale: Open, place, push shut — the same gesture as every kitchen drawer.

ideas.title: Wave-to-open proximity door release

new_nodes.label: Capacitive proximity door release
new_nodes.detail: Solenoid latch opens when a hand approaches, like a sensor bin.

ideas.rationale: Hands full with a hot plate? No button to press.

ideas.title: Mechanical RF shutter replaces electrical interlock logic

new_nodes.label: Door-driven waveguide shutter
new_nodes.detail: Opening the door mechanically slides a metal shutter across the waveguide, blocking RF regardless of electronics.

ideas.rationale: Intrinsic safety needs no explanation and no user caution.

ideas.title: Hinge contacts as the interlock

new_nodes.label: Conductive hinge-pin interlock
new_nodes.detail: Door hinge completes the magnetron circuit only when fully closed.

ideas.rationale: Fewer parts to fail or confuse, keeping the appliance trouble-free.

ideas.title: Optical door-closed sensor replaces monitor switch

new_nodes.label: Reflective optical door sensor
new_nodes.detail: IR LED/phototransistor pair confirms door seating as the monitor channel.

ideas.rationale: Removes the 'door not quite shut' confusion by sensing seating directly.

ideas.title: Conductive mesh gasket replaces quarter-wave choke

new_nodes.label: Knitted-wire RF gasket
new_nodes.detail: Compressible metal mesh seals RF at the door rim with simpler stamping.

ideas.rationale: Cheaper manufacture funds a simpler, better-labelled front panel.

ideas.title: Transparent conductive glass door (no mesh, no lamp)

new_nodes.label: ITO-coated full-glass door
new_nodes.detail: Transparent conductive oxide film shields RF while giving an unobstructed view by room light.

ideas.rationale: Seeing clearly means fewer mistakes without reading any display.

ideas.title: Transparent mesh cavity 'pod'

new_nodes.label: Fine-mesh see-through cavity
new_nodes.detail: Entire cavity is fine Faraday mesh in a plastic shell; food is visible from all sides.

ideas.rationale: Total visibility replaces the need for feedback displays.

ideas.title: LED strip in door frame replaces incandescent lamp

new_nodes.label: Door-frame LED strip
new_nodes.detail: Cool, long-life LEDs outside the RF cavity light the food through the window.

ideas.rationale: A bulb the user never has to replace means no maintenance to learn.

ideas.title: Window glows green when done, replacing the bell

new_nodes.label: Colour-shifting edge-lit window
new_nodes.detail: Window lights amber while heating, green when finished.

ideas.rationale: Status is understood at a glance across the room without sound or text.

ideas.title: Spoken 'Done' replaces the bell

new_nodes.label: Voice-prompt speaker
new_nodes.detail: Plays short spoken cues: 'heating', 'done', 'let it stand'.

ideas.rationale: Plain words beat symbolic beeps for first-time users.

ideas.title: Talking knob: audio hints when touched

new_nodes.label: Touch-triggered audio guidance
new_nodes.detail: Touching any control speaks what it does and a suggested setting.

ideas.rationale: Replaces the printed manual with just-in-time spoken help.

ideas.title: Pull-string timer (pull length = heating time)

new_nodes.label: Retracting pull-cord timer
new_nodes.detail: Pull the cord out to a marked length; it retracts slowly and stops the oven at zero, like a toy.

ideas.rationale: A playful, bodily gesture replaces reading a dial.

ideas.title: Hourglass sand timer as the visible clock

new_nodes.label: Flip-hourglass with optical end sensor
new_nodes.detail: Flip the glass to start; a sensor stops the magnetron when sand runs out.

ideas.rationale: The remaining time is literally visible, no numbers required.

ideas.title: Hand-crank energy timer

new_nodes.label: Wind-up crank timer
new_nodes.detail: Number of crank turns sets both the clockwork timer and the power cam together.

ideas.rationale: More cranking = more heating, an intuitive physical metaphor.

ideas.title: Detented 'coffee / soup / dinner' presets on the timer knob

new_nodes.label: Timer knob with labelled hard detents
new_nodes.detail: Mechanical clicks at 45 s, 2 min, 4 min with icon labels.

new_edges.from: Timer knob with labelled hard detents
Timer knob with labelled hard detents

ideas.rationale: Cheap fix: the right short setting snaps into place without guessing.

ideas.title: Foot-pedal start for hands-full users

new_nodes.label: Kick-plate start/stop pedal
new_nodes.detail: Toe-operated plate at the base starts and stops heating.

ideas.rationale: One obvious control that works even with hands occupied.

ideas.title: Camera in the door replaces lamp and window grid

new_nodes.label: Internal camera with small door display
new_nodes.detail: Shows food live and flags boiling-over automatically.

new_edges.from: Internal camera with small door display
Internal camera with small door display

ideas.rationale: Automatic mistake detection means the user needs no technique.

ideas.title: Built-in stir stick prevents superheating

new_nodes.label: Ceramic nucleation stick in cavity
new_nodes.detail: A rough ceramic rod the user drops in any mug; no need to know about superheating.

ideas.rationale: Substitutes user knowledge with a physical object.

ideas.title: Non-metallic cavity liner immune to arcing

new_nodes.label: Arc-detecting auto-cutoff
new_nodes.detail: Microphone/current sensor detects arcing and shuts off before damage.

ideas.rationale: Users need not learn the 'no metal' rule; the oven forgives them.

ideas.title: Retractable cord replaces loose cord and plug

new_nodes.label: Spring-retract cord reel
new_nodes.detail: Vacuum-cleaner-style cord reel in the base.

ideas.rationale: Set-up is plug in and go; no cable to manage in a dorm.

ideas.title: Wall-plug microwave (plug built into the casing)

new_nodes.label: Integral wall-mount plug chassis
new_nodes.detail: A small 300 W unit that hangs directly on the socket like a night-light.

ideas.rationale: No installation decisions at all: hang it on the wall socket.

ideas.title: USB-C PD 'slow microwave' for mugs

new_nodes.label: 100 W USB-C powered mini cavity
new_nodes.detail: Solid-state RF mug warmer powered by a laptop charger.

new_nodes.label: Portable heating anywhere
new_nodes.detail: Dorm, office, car.

ideas.rationale: One button, one cable students already own.

ideas.title: Door-close equals start

new_nodes.label: Auto-start on door close
new_nodes.detail: Closing the door begins a sensor-controlled cycle; opening it stops.

ideas.rationale: The only action is opening and closing the door.

ideas.title: Big single knob: turn to start, press to stop

new_nodes.label: Oversized rotary-push controller
new_nodes.detail: A single large knob with pictograms; turning starts, pushing stops, nothing else.

ideas.rationale: Two knobs and a button collapse into one obvious control.

ideas.title: One Big Button (30 s per press)

new_nodes.label: Single oversized add-30s button
new_nodes.detail: Each press adds 30 s at full power; nothing else to set.

new_nodes.label: Single-chip pulse-count timer
new_nodes.detail: Cheap 8-pin MCU counts presses, drives relay and buzzer.

ideas.rationale: Two knobs collapse into one obvious action anyone can perform without reading.

ideas.title: Hold-to-Heat Dead-Man Button

new_nodes.label: Hold-to-heat momentary switch
new_nodes.detail: Magnetron runs only while the button is held; release stops it.

ideas.rationale: No duration to think about: user watches the food and simply lets go when done.

ideas.title: Hourglass Timer

new_nodes.label: Flip-over sand hourglass timer module
new_nodes.detail: User flips a sand glass; an optical gate under the lower bulb cuts power when sand finishes.

new_nodes.label: Granular-flow optical gating
new_nodes.detail: Photo-interrupter sees sand column empty and opens magnetron relay.

ideas.rationale: A universally understood object replaces a numbered dial; the remaining sand shows progress at a glance.

ideas.title: Water-Clock Drip Timer

new_nodes.label: Drip-fed float timer
new_nodes.detail: User pours a cup of water into a funnel; drip rate drains it, float drops and opens contacts.

ideas.rationale: Mains-frequency independent and visually self-explaining: more water equals more time.

ideas.title: Pull-String Toy Timer

new_nodes.label: Pull-string spring-return timer
new_nodes.detail: Pull a cord out; it retracts over minutes via an escapement and breaks the circuit at home.

ideas.rationale: A single gross-motor pull with visible string length as the time display suits elderly hands.

ideas.title: Linear 'Longer' Slider

new_nodes.label: Long linear slider timer
new_nodes.detail: A 25 cm slide potentiometer labelled only 'shorter ↔ longer' sets duration; slider creeps back to zero.

ideas.rationale: Linear travel maps directly to time, is readable from across the room, and has fine short-duration resolution.

ideas.title: Food-Icon Wheel Instead of Minutes

new_nodes.label: Pictogram selector wheel
new_nodes.detail: Dial shows only pictures (cup, plate, bowl, frozen block); each hard-wires a time/power pair.

ideas.rationale: Users pick what they have, not numbers, eliminating any mental conversion.

ideas.title: Weighing Turntable Sets Time

new_nodes.label: Load-cell turntable auto-timer
new_nodes.detail: Turntable weighs the dish; time is derived from mass, start on door close.

new_nodes.label: Strain-gauge weighing
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost load cell under turntable motor.

ideas.rationale: Zero settings: put food in, close door, it heats proportionally to how much is there.

ideas.title: Steam-Stop Auto Timer

new_nodes.label: Humidity-burst cutoff sensor
new_nodes.detail: Cavity vent humidity sensor stops heating when steam release peaks.

ideas.rationale: Replaces the timer with a sensor so the user never sets a duration at all.

ideas.title: IR Thermometer 'Warm / Hot' Knob

new_nodes.label: Target-temperature knob with IR pyrometer
new_nodes.detail: Two-position knob 'warm' / 'hot'; non-contact IR sensor stops heating at target.

ideas.rationale: People think in 'how hot', not 'how many minutes at what %'; the oven does the translation.

ideas.title: Thermal-Camera Closed Loop, No Controls

new_nodes.label: Low-res thermal array controller
new_nodes.detail: 8x8 thermopile watches dish, pulses magnetron until uniform target temp.

new_nodes.label: Thermopile array imaging
new_nodes.detail: Sub-$5 MEMS thermopile sensor.

ideas.rationale: The entire control panel disappears; close door and it finishes when food is evenly hot.

ideas.title: Door-Close Starts, Door-Open Stops

new_nodes.label: Door-as-switch fixed-dose controller
new_nodes.detail: Closing the door fires a fixed 60 s burst; opening cancels; close again for another.

ideas.rationale: The only interaction the user already must perform—closing the door—becomes the only control.

ideas.title: Gentle/Fast Rocker Replaces 5-Step Power Knob

new_nodes.label: Two-position gentle/fast rocker
new_nodes.detail: Rocker selects 30% or 100% duty via a single bimetal flasher.

ideas.rationale: Five ambiguous power steps become one binary choice with plain words.

ideas.title: Continuous Inverter Dial 'Low ↔ High'

new_nodes.label: Inverter continuous magnetron drive
new_nodes.detail: Switch-mode supply varies anode current for true continuous power.

new_nodes.label: Unmarked low-high analogue dial
new_nodes.detail: Potentiometer with no numbers, like a stove knob.

ideas.rationale: Behaves exactly like a hob knob everyone already knows.

ideas.title: Height-Shelf Power Control

new_nodes.label: Three-level insert shelf
new_nodes.detail: Food placed higher or lower in the cavity receives more or less field; no electrical power setting.

ideas.rationale: Power becomes a physical placement decision ('top shelf = fast') with no knob to learn.

ideas.title: Delete the Power Knob Entirely

new_nodes.label: Fixed 500 W always-on setting
new_nodes.detail: Magnetron sized to a medium power that reheats without needing defrost modes.

ideas.rationale: One fewer control is the simplest control.

ideas.title: Recipe Punch-Card Slot

new_nodes.label: Notched card reader slot
new_nodes.detail: Insert a stiff card (sold with food or printed) whose edge notches set time and power mechanically.

ideas.rationale: Settings come pre-made; the user only pushes a card in.

ideas.title: Barcode-on-Packaging Scanner

new_nodes.label: Door-mounted barcode scanner
new_nodes.detail: Hold the ready-meal under the scanner; GS1 code maps to stored time/power.

ideas.rationale: No reading of pack instructions or dial numbers; scan and go.

ideas.title: NFC Tag Reader in Turntable

new_nodes.label: Turntable NFC reader
new_nodes.detail: Tagged packaging or dishes placed on the turntable transmit cook settings.

new_nodes.label: Passive NFC tagging
new_nodes.detail: 13.56 MHz coil under glass plate; tags cost cents.

ideas.rationale: Placing the food is the whole interaction.

ideas.title: Voice-Only Control

new_nodes.label: Offline keyword speech module
new_nodes.detail: Recognises 'two minutes', 'stop', 'defrost' locally; no panel.

ideas.rationale: Speaking a duration is the most natural interface for users who struggle with knobs.

ideas.title: Wave-to-Add-Time Gesture Sensor

new_nodes.label: IR gesture bar
new_nodes.detail: Each hand wave past the front adds 30 s; wave backwards cancels.

ideas.rationale: Touch-free, no fine motor skills, one gesture to learn.

ideas.title: Joystick Combined Time/Power

new_nodes.label: Single 2-axis joystick
new_nodes.detail: Push forward for longer, sideways for stronger; spring-centre starts.

ideas.rationale: Two parameters, one hand, one object.

ideas.title: Quantity Dial Instead of Time

new_nodes.label: 'How much food' dial
new_nodes.detail: Dial graduated in cups/plates; fixed power; time computed internally.

ideas.rationale: Users estimate quantity far more easily than cooking seconds.

ideas.title: Turntable-Revolution Counter Timer

new_nodes.label: Revolution-count stop dial
new_nodes.detail: Dial sets 'number of turns' (1-10); a reed switch on the turntable counts down.

ideas.rationale: Progress is literally visible as the plate turns; no abstract minutes.

ideas.title: Quartz Electronic Timer Replaces Synchronous Motor

new_nodes.label: Crystal-oscillator timing IC
new_nodes.detail: 32 kHz crystal timer independent of mains frequency; same knob, better accuracy.

ideas.rationale: Keeps the familiar knob but makes short times reliable so first-try results are right.

ideas.title: Bimetal Thermal Timer

new_nodes.label: Heated bimetal delay switch
new_nodes.detail: Knob sets contact gap; a heater coil warps bimetal until contacts open—no motor.

ideas.rationale: Simpler, cheaper mechanism with the same one-knob operation.

ideas.title: Hydraulic Dashpot Timer

new_nodes.label: Oil-damped piston timer
new_nodes.detail: Knob compresses a spring against a viscous dashpot; slow return opens contacts.

ideas.rationale: Silent, motorless and voltage-independent while keeping the familiar twist.

ideas.title: Egg-Timer Dock

new_nodes.label: Removable kitchen egg-timer cradle
new_nodes.detail: Any wind-up egg timer drops into a cradle whose ring-detect mic/latch stops the oven.

ideas.rationale: Users bring the timer they already know how to use.

ideas.title: Coin-Slot Duration Tokens

new_nodes.label: Token slot timer
new_nodes.detail: Drop colour-coded plastic tokens (1 min, 5 min) in a slot; each token trips a fixed delay.

ideas.rationale: Tangible countable units replace reading a scale.

ideas.title: Spoken 'Done' Instead of Bell

new_nodes.label: Voice chip end-of-cycle announcer
new_nodes.detail: Replaces mechanical bell with a sound chip saying 'Your food is ready'.

ideas.rationale: Unambiguous feedback removes guessing about what the ding meant.

ideas.title: Lift-Off Magnetic Door Panel

new_nodes.label: Hinge-less magnetically seated door plate
new_nodes.detail: Door is a flat shielded plate held by magnets and choke flange; lift it off with one hand.

ideas.rationale: No button, no swing arc, no latch to learn—just pick up the lid.

ideas.title: Pull Handle with Magnetic Catch

new_nodes.label: Grab-handle magnetic catch
new_nodes.detail: Door held shut by magnets and interlock reed switch; pulling the handle opens it.

ideas.rationale: Works like a fridge door, the most familiar door in any kitchen.

ideas.title: Drawer Cavity

new_nodes.label: Pull-out drawer cavity
new_nodes.detail: Whole cavity floor slides out like a drawer; shielding by choke rails.

ideas.rationale: Food is loaded from above with no reaching into a box; drawers need no instruction.

ideas.title: Top-Loading Well with Lid

new_nodes.label: Top-loading shielded well
new_nodes.detail: Cylindrical cavity opened from the top with a hinged lid like a rice cooker.

ideas.rationale: Drop-in loading is intuitive and gravity keeps the lid sealed.

ideas.title: Toaster-Style Pop-Up Cavity

new_nodes.label: Pop-up lift cage
new_nodes.detail: Push the cage down to start; a spring-latch timer pops the food up when done.

ideas.rationale: Everyone can use a toaster; start and finish are one physical motion.

ideas.title: Rotating Carousel Cavity

new_nodes.label: Rotate-out turret cavity
new_nodes.detail: Cavity is a drum that turns 180° to present its open side; closed position seals against choke.

ideas.rationale: Turn to load, turn to cook—a single rotary motion with no door at all.

ideas.title: Chain-Mail Curtain Door

new_nodes.label: Conductive mesh roller curtain
new_nodes.detail: Fine stainless chain-mail curtain rolls up like a blind; edges run in grounded tracks.

ideas.rationale: No swing clearance and no latch; push it up like a blind.

ideas.title: Garage-Style Roll-Up Shutter

new_nodes.label: Segmented steel roll-up shutter
new_nodes.detail: Interlocking stamped slats roll into the top; closing completes the interlock.

ideas.rationale: One up/down motion with nothing protruding into the user's space.

ideas.title: Drop-Down Oven Door

new_nodes.label: Bottom-hinged fold-down door
new_nodes.detail: Door folds down to form a shelf for dishes, like a conventional oven.

ideas.rationale: Mirrors the oven people already own and gives a landing spot for hot plates.

ideas.title: Foot-Pedal Door Opener

new_nodes.label: Foot pedal latch release
new_nodes.detail: Pedal at base pulls a Bowden cable to the latch lever.

ideas.rationale: Hands-full users open the door without finding a small button.

ideas.title: Elbow Paddle Release

new_nodes.label: Full-height side paddle
new_nodes.detail: A long bar down the door edge releases the latch when nudged anywhere.

ideas.rationale: Impossible to miss, operable with elbow, wrist or hand.

ideas.title: Proximity Auto-Open Door

new_nodes.label: Capacitive approach auto-latch
new_nodes.detail: After cycle ends, a hand near the door pops the latch via solenoid.

ideas.rationale: The door opens itself; nothing to find or press.

ideas.title: Auto-Open at Bell

new_nodes.label: Timer-cam driven door pop
new_nodes.detail: The same cam that rings the bell also kicks the latch lever so the door swings ajar.

ideas.rationale: 'Done' is signalled by the door itself opening—no button and no bell to interpret.

ideas.title: Gravity Latch

new_nodes.label: Gravity-drop hook latch
new_nodes.detail: A weighted hook falls into the keeper on close; lifting the door handle slightly frees it.

ideas.rationale: No spring, no button: lift and pull is self-evident.

ideas.title: Transparent Conductive Film Window

new_nodes.label: ITO / silver-nanowire shielding glass
new_nodes.detail: Fully clear glass pane with transparent conductive coating replaces perforated mesh.

ideas.rationale: A clear view of the food lets users judge doneness without understanding settings.

ideas.title: Mesh-Embedded Polymer Door

new_nodes.label: Insert-moulded mesh polycarbonate
new_nodes.detail: Mesh overmoulded in a single clear polymer shot forms the whole door, no glass, no steel frame.

ideas.rationale: Lighter door is easier to swing for elderly users and cheaper to build.

ideas.title: Living-Hinge Flexible Door

new_nodes.label: Conductive-silicone living hinge
new_nodes.detail: Door attached by a flexible conductive elastomer strip; no pins or stamped hinges.

ideas.rationale: Door flops open any way it is pushed; nothing to align or jam.

ideas.title: Faraday Cloche Over a Hot-Plate Base

new_nodes.detail: Magnetron in a base plate; a metal-mesh dome cloche placed over the dish completes the cage and interlock.

ideas.rationale: Cover the plate, it heats; lift the cover, it stops—no box, no door, no buttons.

ideas.title: Tip-Out Serving Tray at End

new_nodes.label: Timer-released tilting tray
new_nodes.detail: Cam end-stop releases a tilt tray that slides the dish forward through a flap for pickup.

ideas.rationale: The oven hands the food back; the user never operates the door.

ideas.title: Remote Key-Fob Start

new_nodes.detail: Car-key style fob replaces panel; Go = 1 min full power each press.

ideas.title: Thermochromic Cavity Floor as Timer Display

ideas.title: Cook-until-hot button

new_nodes.label: Thermopile IR food-temperature sensing
new_nodes.detail: Non-contact IR element views the turntable through a waveguide-safe window.

ideas.rationale: Removes both knobs so the only decision is 'press'; serves M6 directly.

ideas.title: Weigh-and-go timer

new_nodes.label: Load-cell turntable auto-timer
new_nodes.detail: Food mass sets duration automatically via a mechanical spring scale coupled to the timer cam.

ideas.rationale: User never chooses a time; weight decides it, so zero learning.

ideas.title: Hourglass timer

new_nodes.label: Flip-over sand hourglass with optical end sensor
new_nodes.detail: Flipping the glass starts heating; empty upper bulb trips a photo-interrupter.

new_edges.from: Flip-over sand hourglass with optical end sensor
Flip-over sand hourglass with optical end sensor

ideas.rationale: Everyone already understands an hourglass; the control is self-explanatory.

ideas.title: Pull-string timer

new_nodes.label: Pull-cord spring timer
new_nodes.detail: Pull the cord out; its retraction length equals cooking time, like a toy.

ideas.rationale: A single intuitive gesture replaces reading a dial.

ideas.title: Toaster lever start

Push-down lever that pops up when done
Push-down lever that pops up when done

ideas.title: Hold-to-heat paddle

new_nodes.label: Dead-man's paddle switch
new_nodes.detail: Magnetron runs only while the big paddle is held; release stops it.

ideas.rationale: No numbers at all; user watches food and lets go.

ideas.title: Pictogram dial

new_nodes.label: Food-icon selector dial
new_nodes.detail: Cup, plate, popcorn, frozen icons map to fixed time/power cams.

ideas.rationale: Users pick what they are heating instead of how.

ideas.title: One-minute tally button

new_nodes.label: Add-a-minute ratchet button

ideas.title: Package tag auto-set

new_nodes.detail: Reads heating instructions printed on the food packaging.

new_nodes.label: Low-cost NFC reader IC
new_nodes.detail: Near-field tag reading through plastic packaging.

ideas.rationale: Food tells the oven what to do; user just loads it.

ideas.title: Turn-count dial

new_nodes.label: Turntable-revolution counter dial
new_nodes.detail: User selects 'how many turns'; a cam on the turntable motor counts them.

ideas.rationale: Visible rotations are easier to grasp than abstract minutes.

ideas.title: Shelf-height power

new_nodes.detail: Raising/lowering food in the standing-wave field changes absorbed power continuously.

new_nodes.detail: A lever slides a plate partially over the feed aperture, attenuating power continuously.

ideas.title: Gentle/Fast toggle

Warm/Hot/Boiling thermostat dial with IR sensor

ideas.title: Drawer microwave

new_nodes.detail: Whole cavity floor slides out on rails; choke flange seals when closed.

ideas.title: Top-loading lid

ideas.title: Roll-shutter door

ideas.title: Sideways pocket door

new_nodes.detail: Door slides into the side wall on a rail; no hinge or latch lever.

ideas.rationale: One linear motion replaces button-plus-swing.

ideas.title: Revolving-drum loader

new_nodes.detail: Turn the drum to expose the shelf, turn back to seal; the drum wall is the door.

ideas.title: Iris aperture door

ideas.title: Conductive clear door

new_nodes.detail: Transparent conductive film blocks 2.45 GHz without a perforated mesh.

ideas.title: Hourglass timer

new_nodes.label: Flip-over sand hourglass with tilt switch
new_nodes.detail: Flipping the glass closes a switch; when sand runs out a float drops and opens it.

new_edges.from: Flip-over sand hourglass with tilt switch
Flip-over sand hourglass with tilt switch

ideas.rationale: Everyone already understands an hourglass; no numbers or dials to learn.

ideas.title: Doneness slider

new_nodes.label: Single 'cold→hot' linear slider
new_nodes.detail: One potentiometer maps to a combined time×power profile.

ideas.rationale: Collapses two controls into one intuitive 'how hot do you want it' gesture.

ideas.title: Weigh-to-cook turntable

new_nodes.label: Load cell under turntable auto-setting duration
new_nodes.detail: Food mass sets heating time by a fixed J/g rule; no user input.

new_edges.from: Load cell under turntable auto-setting duration
Load cell under turntable auto-setting duration

ideas.rationale: User just puts food in and closes the door—zero settings.

ideas.title: IR thermometer stop

new_nodes.label: Thermopile IR surface-temperature sensing
new_nodes.detail: Sensor in cavity roof stops magnetron when food reaches a target temperature.

new_nodes.label: Three-icon 'warm / hot / boiling' selector
new_nodes.detail: Replaces minutes with a target temperature.

ideas.rationale: Users think in 'hot enough', not minutes—removes guesswork.

ideas.title: Steam-stop sensor

new_nodes.label: Humidity sensor in exhaust vent, stops on steam burst
new_nodes.detail: Cheap capacitive humidity sensor replaces timing logic.

new_edges.from: Humidity sensor in exhaust vent, stops on steam burst
Humidity sensor in exhaust vent, stops on steam burst

ideas.rationale: Press start and walk away; the oven decides when it's done.

ideas.title: Voice-only control

new_nodes.label: Offline keyword speech recognition
new_nodes.detail: Low-cost MCU recognises 'heat', 'defrost', 'stop'.

new_nodes.label: Microphone replacing both knobs
new_nodes.detail: No front-panel controls at all.

ideas.rationale: Speaking is the most natural interface, ideal for elderly or visually impaired users.

ideas.title: Pull-string timer

new_nodes.label: Wind-up pull cord (pull length = cooking time)
new_nodes.detail: Toy-style string spring motor drives the cam shaft.

new_edges.from: Wind-up pull cord (pull length = cooking time)
Wind-up pull cord (pull length = cooking time)

ideas.rationale: Pulling a cord is a universal, self-explanatory gesture.

ideas.title: Food-icon dial

new_nodes.label: Dial with pictograms (cup, plate, pizza, frozen) instead of minutes
new_nodes.detail: Each detent selects a fixed time/power preset.

new_edges.from: Dial with pictograms (cup, plate, pizza, frozen) instead of minutes
Dial with pictograms (cup, plate, pizza, frozen) instead of minutes

ideas.rationale: Removes the need to know how many minutes anything takes.

ideas.title: Package barcode reader

new_nodes.label: Barcode/NFC scanner in door frame reads package heating instructions
new_nodes.detail: Cooking program comes from the product label.

new_edges.from: Barcode/NFC scanner in door frame reads package heating instructions
Barcode/NFC scanner in door frame reads package heating instructions

ideas.rationale: Scan and go—no reading of instructions or setting of controls.

ideas.title: Camera food recognition

new_nodes.label: On-device image classification
new_nodes.detail: Tiny neural net recognises food type and portion.

new_nodes.label: Cavity camera replacing the timer
new_nodes.detail: Auto-selects program on door close.

ideas.rationale: The oven does the thinking; the user does nothing but close the door.

ideas.title: No power knob at all

new_nodes.label: Fixed full-power operation (knob deleted)
new_nodes.detail: Removes cam switch; defrost handled by longer time at intermittent magnetron via timer cam.

ideas.rationale: Fewer controls means literally nothing to learn and lower BOM.

ideas.title: Inverter gentle/fast rocker

new_nodes.label: Inverter continuous power control
new_nodes.detail: Switch-mode HV supply varies magnetron output continuously.

new_nodes.label: Two-position 'gentle / fast' rocker switch
new_nodes.detail: Replaces 5-step cam.

ideas.rationale: Binary choice in plain words is instantly understood.

ideas.title: Defrost/cook slide

new_nodes.label: Two-position slide switch 'defrost / cook'
new_nodes.detail: Single cam position swap, cheaper than 5-step.

ideas.rationale: Reduces a five-way decision to the only two most people ever use.

ideas.title: Gravity pendulum timer

new_nodes.label: Weighted swing arm timer (lift arm, it falls slowly via dashpot)
new_nodes.detail: Oil dashpot sets rate; arm position shows remaining time.

new_edges.from: Weighted swing arm timer (lift arm, it falls slowly via dashpot)
Weighted swing arm timer (lift arm, it falls slowly via dashpot)

ideas.rationale: Visual, tactile, mains-frequency-independent and obvious to use.

ideas.title: Foot pedal door

new_nodes.label: Foot pedal door release
new_nodes.detail: Bowden cable to latch lever like a pedal bin.

ideas.rationale: Hands-full opening with a gesture everyone knows from pedal bins.

ideas.title: Magnetic pull door

new_nodes.label: Magnet-held door with handle and reed-switch interlock
new_nodes.detail: No latch, no button; just pull.

new_edges.from: Magnet-held door with handle and reed-switch interlock
Magnet-held door with handle and reed-switch interlock

ideas.rationale: Works like a fridge door—zero instruction needed.

ideas.title: Roll-top tambour door

new_nodes.label: Metal tambour roll-top door with conductive slats
new_nodes.detail: Slides up into the housing; no swing clearance, no hinges.

new_edges.from: Metal tambour roll-top door with conductive slats
Metal tambour roll-top door with conductive slats

ideas.rationale: Push up to open, pull down to close—intuitive and space-saving.

ideas.title: Drawer microwave

new_nodes.label: Pull-out drawer cavity with choke seal
new_nodes.detail: The whole cavity floor slides out like a kitchen drawer.

new_edges.from: Pull-out drawer cavity with choke seal
Pull-out drawer cavity with choke seal

ideas.rationale: Drawers are universally understood and let elderly users load from above.

ideas.title: Auto-open at end

new_nodes.label: Solenoid auto-pop door at end of cycle
new_nodes.detail: Replaces bell: the open door is the signal.

new_edges.from: Solenoid auto-pop door at end of cycle
Solenoid auto-pop door at end of cycle

ideas.rationale: Done means open; no bell to interpret, no button to find.

ideas.title: Top-loading toaster style

new_nodes.label: Top lid with spring-loaded lift platform
new_nodes.detail: Food sits on a platform that rises when done, like a toaster.

new_edges.from: Top lid with spring-loaded lift platform
Top lid with spring-loaded lift platform

ideas.rationale: Borrows a mental model everyone already has from toasters.

ideas.title: Wave-to-open sensor

new_nodes.label: Capacitive/IR proximity sensor triggering latch solenoid
new_nodes.detail: Wave a hand in front of the door to open.

new_edges.from: Capacitive/IR proximity sensor triggering latch solenoid

ideas.rationale: No button to locate or press force needed—good for arthritic hands.

ideas.title: Conveyor tunnel, no door

new_nodes.label: Waveguide-below-cutoff entry tunnels
new_nodes.detail: Long narrow tunnels attenuate leakage without any door.

new_nodes.label: Pass-through belt tunnel oven
new_nodes.detail: Food goes in one side, comes out heated the other.

ideas.rationale: Place plate on belt and it comes out hot—no door, no knobs.

ideas.title: One-lever open-and-start

new_nodes.label: Big lever: pull to open door, push to close and start fixed cycle
new_nodes.detail: Lever stroke winds a fixed 1-min spring timer.

new_edges.from: Big lever: pull to open door, push to close and start fixed cycle
Big lever: pull to open door, push to close and start fixed cycle

ideas.rationale: Whole interaction is one physical motion.

ideas.title: Transparent conductive glass door

new_nodes.label: ITO / metal-mesh-on-glass transparent shielding
new_nodes.detail: Conductive coating gives Faraday shielding with clear view.

ideas.rationale: Clear view lets users judge doneness by eye without learning timings.

ideas.title: Thermochromic door panel

new_nodes.label: Thermochromic strip on door showing cavity/food heat colour
new_nodes.detail: Blue→red colour change replaces readouts.

new_edges.from: Thermochromic strip on door showing cavity/food heat colour
Thermochromic strip on door showing cavity/food heat colour

ideas.rationale: Colour is a universal, language-free indicator of 'hot'.

ideas.title: Knock-to-set

new_nodes.label: Piezo knock sensor on cabinet (each knock = 30 s)
new_nodes.detail: No knobs; knock the top to add time.

new_edges.from: Piezo knock sensor on cabinet (each knock = 30 s)

ideas.rationale: Playful, discoverable, and needs no panel at all.

ideas.title: Dedicated cup slot

new_nodes.label: Cup-shaped docking recess with limit switch auto-starting a mug program
new_nodes.detail: Drop in a mug; it heats to drinking temp.

new_edges.from: Cup-shaped docking recess with limit switch auto-starting a mug program

ideas.rationale: Form dictates function—the slot only fits one thing and does one thing.

ideas.title: Plate-size detection

new_nodes.label: Optical plate-diameter sensor setting time
new_nodes.detail: Bigger plate = longer heat, no input needed.

ideas.rationale: Removes the time decision for the most common use case.

ideas.title: Big-number egg timer

new_nodes.label: Oversized wind-up kitchen-timer knob with 3 cm tactile digits
new_nodes.detail: Same cam tech, redesigned for legibility and grip.

new_edges.from: Oversized wind-up kitchen-timer knob with 3 cm tactile digits
Oversized wind-up kitchen-timer knob with 3 cm tactile digits

ideas.rationale: Keeps the familiar knob but makes it readable and grippable for elderly users.

ideas.title: Colour-band dial

new_nodes.label: Timer dial with green/yellow/red bands instead of numbers
new_nodes.detail: Short/medium/long encoded as colour.

new_edges.from: Timer dial with green/yellow/red bands instead of numbers

ideas.rationale: Eliminates numeracy and language from the interface.

ideas.title: Hold-to-heat dead-man button

new_nodes.label: Hold-down 'heat while pressed' palm button
new_nodes.detail: Magnetron runs only while the button is held; release to stop.

ideas.rationale: Direct cause-and-effect control with no timing abstraction.

ideas.title: Swipe-length touch strip

new_nodes.label: Capacitive strip—swipe length sets minutes, LEDs count down
new_nodes.detail: No moving parts.

new_edges.from: Capacitive strip—swipe length sets minutes, LEDs count down
Capacitive strip—swipe length sets minutes, LEDs count down

ideas.rationale: Longer swipe = longer cook is self-explanatory and precise for short times.

ideas.title: Food-shaped preset buttons

new_nodes.label: Four physical buttons moulded as mug, plate, pizza slice, snowflake
new_nodes.detail: Shape tells function; each triggers a fixed program.

new_edges.from: Four physical buttons moulded as mug, plate, pizza slice, snowflake
Four physical buttons moulded as mug, plate, pizza slice, snowflake

ideas.rationale: Tactile icons are usable without sight or language.

ideas.title: 30-s detent dial

new_nodes.label: Detented timer dial with 30-s clicks up to 5 min, coarse beyond
new_nodes.detail: Non-linear cam profile.

new_edges.from: Detented timer dial with 30-s clicks up to 5 min, coarse beyond
Detented timer dial with 30-s clicks up to 5 min, coarse beyond

ideas.rationale: Clicks give haptic certainty for the short times people actually use.

ideas.title: Light signal instead of bell

new_nodes.label: Flashing cavity lamp at end of cycle replacing bell
new_nodes.detail: Reuses existing lamp; no bell striker.

new_edges.from: Flashing cavity lamp at end of cycle replacing bell
Flashing cavity lamp at end of cycle replacing bell

ideas.rationale: Visible-from-across-room 'done' signal, fewer parts.

ideas.title: Rotating drum door

new_nodes.label: Rotating cylindrical cavity with open sector that turns to face user
new_nodes.detail: Spin the drum to load; spin back to seal.

new_edges.from: Rotating cylindrical cavity with open sector that turns to face user
Rotating cylindrical cavity with open sector that turns to face user

ideas.rationale: One rotary motion replaces door, button and latch.

ideas.title: Rice-cooker lid

new_nodes.label: Hinged top lid with magnetic catch, cavity loaded from above
new_nodes.detail: Lid is a flat steel pan with choke rim.

new_edges.from: Hinged top lid with magnetic catch, cavity loaded from above

ideas.rationale: Lid-pot mental model is universal across cultures.

ideas.title: Sensitivity dial for sensor

new_nodes.label: Single 'a bit less / a bit more' trim dial for auto-sensor cooking
new_nodes.detail: Replaces power knob once sensing takes over.

new_edges.from: Single 'a bit less / a bit more' trim dial for auto-sensor cooking

ideas.rationale: User only ever expresses preference, never technical settings.

ideas.title: Spring-scale timer

new_nodes.label: Turntable on spring that mechanically winds timer by food weight
new_nodes.detail: Purely mechanical weight-to-time linkage.

new_edges.from: Turntable on spring that mechanically winds timer by food weight
Turntable on spring that mechanically winds timer by food weight

ideas.rationale: Automatic timing with no electronics and nothing to set.

ideas.title: Temperature probe plug

new_nodes.label: Shielded food probe with single 'eat' button
new_nodes.detail: Stops at 70 °C core temperature.

new_edges.from: Shielded food probe with single 'eat' button
Shielded food probe with single 'eat' button

ideas.rationale: Guarantees food is safely hot without any timing knowledge.

ideas.title: Pull-cord door

new_nodes.label: Dangling pull cord releasing door latch
new_nodes.detail: Cord on front lifts the latch lever.

new_edges.from: Dangling pull cord releasing door latch

ideas.rationale: Tug-to-open is obvious and works with elbows or bandaged hands.

ideas.title: Pass-through two-door oven

new_nodes.label: Doors on both front and back for hatch installation
new_nodes.detail: Second door shares hinge/latch tooling.

new_edges.from: Doors on both front and back for hatch installation

ideas.rationale: Load from kitchen, retrieve at table—no juggling the hot plate.

ideas.title: Metal-fibre polymer window

new_nodes.label: Injection-moulded polymer with embedded conductive fibre mesh
new_nodes.detail: One-shot window replaces glass + stamped mesh.

new_edges.from: Injection-moulded polymer with embedded conductive fibre mesh

new_edges.to: Injection-moulded polymer with embedded conductive fibre mesh

new_edges.from: Injection-moulded polymer with embedded conductive fibre mesh

ideas.rationale: Lighter, cheaper door that is easier for elderly users to swing.

ideas.title: Tactile wedge knobs

new_nodes.label: Wedge-shaped knobs with braille and ratchet clicks
new_nodes.detail: Orientation of wedge = setting, felt not seen.

new_edges.from: Wedge-shaped knobs with braille and ratchet clicks
Wedge-shaped knobs with braille and ratchet clicks
Wedge-shaped knobs with braille and ratchet clicks

ideas.rationale: Settings can be confirmed by touch alone.

ideas.title: Push-the-door to open

new_nodes.label: Push-push latch: press door panel to pop it open
new_nodes.detail: Cabinet-style push catch replaces button and lever.

new_edges.from: Push-push latch: press door panel to pop it open
Push-push latch: press door panel to pop it open

ideas.rationale: The door itself is the button—nothing else to find.

ideas.title: Defrost mat

new_nodes.label: Blue silicone mat with RFID tag; placing it triggers defrost duty
new_nodes.detail: Physical token replaces power selection.

new_edges.from: Blue silicone mat with RFID tag; placing it triggers defrost duty

ideas.rationale: Power level becomes a physical object you either use or don't.

ideas.title: Talking oven

new_nodes.label: Speech output chip announcing 'ready' and counting down
new_nodes.detail: Replaces bell with spoken status.

new_edges.from: Speech output chip announcing 'ready' and counting down
Speech output chip announcing 'ready' and counting down

ideas.rationale: Plain-language feedback needs no interpretation of chimes.

ideas.title: Close-to-start door

new_nodes.label: Door-close switch starts a fixed 1-min full-power cycle automatically
new_nodes.detail: Timer knob removed; reopen door to stop.

new_edges.from: Door-close switch starts a fixed 1-min full-power cycle automatically
Door-close switch starts a fixed 1-min full-power cycle automatically

ideas.rationale: The only control is the door—impossible to misuse.

ideas.title: Clear glass cavity

new_nodes.label: Full transparent conductive-coated glass cavity and door
new_nodes.detail: No lamp, no mesh; whole oven is see-through.

new_edges.from: Full transparent conductive-coated glass cavity and door

ideas.rationale: Users monitor food directly from any angle, learning nothing but 'look'.
